name: SikaPlast-70
paste:
SIKAPLAST®-70: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaPlast®-70, July 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sikaplast_-70.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaPlast®-70 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. SikaPlast®-70 is a water reducer specifically formulated for use with harsh manufactured sands or poorly-graded natural sand. SikaPlast®-70 improves the finishability, pumping and slump keeping properties of the fresh concrete.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaPlast®-70 is suitable to produce high performance concrete with poor quality sands. The following types of concrete can use SikaPlast®-70:
    - Mixes containing harsh aggregates and high percentage of manufactured sand
    - Reinforced, precast, prestressed, lightweight, normal weight or pumped concrete.
    - Concrete, where reduced water contents and ease of placing and working with tools is needed.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaPlast®-70
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Mid Range Water Reducer - MWR
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports. SikaPlast®-70 is a medium-range water reducing admixture meeting the requirements of AS1478.1 – 2000 Type MWR.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS1478.1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer. Use of SikaPlast®-70 in concrete improves the following properties:
    - Reduces water, improving concrete durability.
    - Facilitates an increase in manufactured sand or poor quality natural sand.
    - Increased Ultimate Strength Performance.
    - Improved plastic concrete properties.
    - Ease of placing or pumping.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Aqueous solution of modified polycarboxylate
    - Appearance and colour: Blue liquid
    - Specific gravity: 1.05 g/cm³
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Bulk deliveries; 205 litre drum; 10 litre container
    - Shelf life: Stored at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C in unopened original containers, protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is at least one (1) year.
    - Storage conditions: Store at temperature between 5oC and 35oC, protected from direct sunlight .

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (July 2023, Version 01.03) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Compatibility: SikaPlast®-70 can be use in conjunction with most of the Sika Concrete admixture, with the exclusion of Sikament NN. For additional information, please contact your local Sika Representative.
4.3 Recommended dosage. Typical dosage for general concrete production is between 300-600mls per 100kg of total cementitious material. Optimum dosage depends on site condition, job conditions, mix ingredients and desired plastic and hardened properties. Laboratory and field trials are essential in determining the optimum dosage. SikaPlast®-70 can be used at higher doses to achieve a large water cut and increased set times.
4.4 Dispensing. Add SikaPlast®-70 to the initial batching water. For best result, we recommend thorough mixing of wet concrete at 60 seconds per cubic metre of concrete. Add the remaining gauging water progressively after at least 2/3 wet mixing time to achieve the desired consistency. Do not add to a dry mix.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations. When using SikaPlast®-70 setting time will depend on site conditions. This should be checked and predetermined with trial mixes.
4.6 Further information. May slightly increase air content of concrete when used at normal dose.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (July 2023, Version 01.03) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - When using SikaPlast®-70 setting time will depend on site conditions. This should be checked and predetermined with trial mixes.
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaPlast®-70, July 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sikaplast_-70.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaPlast®-70, version 28/10/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sds-sikaplast-70.pdf
    - Environmental Product Declaration: EPD SikaPlast®-70, version 12/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/epd-sikaplast-70.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
